title: A pending backup restore whose copy is gone from the target can be neither finished nor abandoned
outcome: A pending backup restore whose copy is gone from the target can be neither finished nor abandoned
acceptance: The explicit documented command `engram backup restore COPY --abandon-pending --abandoned-by NAME` abandons only a readable pending restore whose copy equals COPY, under the existing store push lock and with no database or sidecars present. It makes no target contact, requires no --origin-retired-by, and never abandons implicitly. Tests show a missing target copy can be abandoned and a restore of another copy then proceeds; ordinary different-copy requests still refuse without abandonment.

Before cleanup the command validates that the exact recorded staging file belongs to this restore inside the intended project directory. It refuses traversal, external paths, directories, symlinks/reparse redirection and inspection errors; an already missing owned stage is allowed. It removes only that recorded owned file, never unrelated files, recursively or by wildcard. Tests cover these refusals and unrelated-file preservation.

Cleanup precedes archival: a cleanup failure leaves the pending record active and blocks abandonment. After cleanup, an archive with a no-replace UTC-stamped name contains format version, abandoned {by, at}, and pending as the original parsed JSON record with every field preserved. The active Pending format/state is unchanged. Archive failure leaves the pending record available for retry and reports that the stage was already removed; abandonment is never called completed. Tests cover cleanup/archive failures and archive-name collisions. Successful archival clears active pending status; the envelope remains readable provenance without adding a history listing.

A restore retry that fetches a replacement stage B verifies it against the pending copy's digest and persists the staging pointer to B before retiring earlier stage A. State-write failure preserves A and its original record, cleans B or names the cleanup failure, and stops; a later format/check refusal leaves B with the record pointing to B. The possible interrupted pointer-switch orphan is disclosed, and no sweep of unrelated files occurs. Regression coverage includes the A-to-B refusal followed by another retry.

The `backup_restore_pending_other` refusal and the pending status line name both the retry and the explicit COPY-bound abandonment command. Help, receipts and relevant backup documentation describe attribution, cleanup, the archive and refusal outcomes accurately; command rendering handles quoted copy/operator names. Tests cover the displayed alternatives and quoting.

completion.summary:
Landed as 3a5a50e.
- `engram backup restore COPY --abandon-pending --abandoned-by NAME` abandons the pending restore of COPY. It runs under the push lock, with no store or sidecar present, never contacts the target, and is never run implicitly.
- It removes only the restore's own staging file. The file must carry its uuid name and lie directly in <home>/projects/<digest>/. That directory and `projects` are opened from the home without following links and held while the file is removed through them; on Windows the removal uses the full path checked against the held handle, so UNC homes work. The removal is then confirmed.
- It archives the pending record whole as store.restore-abandoned-<UTC>Z.json, with the abandoner and the time: written to a tempfile, then moved there without replacing anything. Only after that is the record cleared.
- A retry checks the copy it fetched again against the pending SHA-256, and points the record at it before removing the earlier staging file.
- The pending refusal and the status line name both ways on as `--option=value` commands, quoted for POSIX and PowerShell; the shared quoting is now engram::shell.
Four review rounds. All Highs and Mediums are fixed: R1 ancestor links and the removal race; R1 PowerShell quoting; R3 the UNC relative path. The remaining Low is w-dcaa74469919. Gate test-223321ac passed on freeze 5dd894d5. Independent evaluation 42ac9fc2 passed 5/5. Readiness reported ready on all 4 stores.
The UNC test writes only under the worktree's target/tmp test home; \\localhost\C$ is only a second path to that same directory.
